US500.name: S&P 500

stats.win: ~72% of the 18 new Night V5 legs closed in profit
stats.source: MT4 test SP500_DAYTRADE v1.10 (his run 3 Nov, Magic 500116, spread 18, Every tick), 2019.10.12-2026.10.31, 2,489 trades (+18 vs the 500115 baseline's 2,471); max DD $2,188.15 (0.22%, unchanged from 500115); same 500115 rules (row18/19/20/23/24/25-27) PLUS Night V5 (rows 28-31): a 4th night trigger, no weekday restriction, on the US Dollar Index weakening over 5 days (252-day percentile of the 5-day % change <= 0.20) combined with the market narrowing on both a 10-day AND a 20-day horizon (252-day percentile of the RSP/SPY equal-weight/cap-weight ratio's 10-day and 20-day % change, both <= 0.20) - isolating the 18 new legs alone: net +$401.77, DD unchanged vs 500115, ~72% closed in profit. WATCH ITEM: only 20 historical Python occurrences (18 confirmed in MT4 after excluding nights V2/V3/V4 already took), 70% overlap the Night V2 VIX gate (vs 67.5% baseline - not VIX-in-disguise), 0 loss years across 6 calendar years, survives a stricter trim-robustness check than any earlier leg - treat as a refinement still proving itself, not a settled edge. Unlike Night V4, this data (Yahoo Finance DXY/RSP/SPY) is available from day one - no live warm-up needed (see dxyrs_today() in sp_run.py).

US500.day_note: 14-day range 92 pts · stop 0.75 x range (= 69 pts) · no half-close · the day's first signal sets BUY or SELL, later signals the same way add (max 3 trades) · v1.04: no 2nd/3rd trade from 11:00 am New York or once the day is up half a stop · signals: Nasdaq desk signals copied in US hours + S&P 9:40 am New York move, yesterday high/low sweep, big move by 10 am New York · close 3:30 pm New York · NIGHT trade on high-fear nights (VIX above VIX3M, or VIX / VVIX in their 1-year top 10%): BUY 6:01 pm New York (v1.07: Mon/Tue/Wed broker-days only), stop 1 x range (v1.07, was 2x), close 10:00 am New York · v1.07 TURN-OF-MONTH: on the last broker weekday of the month and the first 3 of the next, BUY 9:30 am New York, stop 0.75 x range, close 3:30 pm New York - only on a day with no other S&P trade · v1.08 NIGHT V3: a 2nd, independent night trigger (only fires when the night trade above does not - never both), broker-day Wed/Thu/Fri only, on a gold+WTI combined overnight shock (the smaller of gold's and WTI's own 252-day-percentile |daily move|, from 2 days before, >= 0.70): BUY 6:01 pm New York, stop 1 x range, close 10:00 am New York - same mechanics as the night leg above · v1.09 NIGHT V4: a 3rd, independent night trigger (only fires when the two night trades above do not - never more than one a night), no weekday restriction, on a weak last-hour close (252-day percentile of the 15:00-16:00 New York return <= 0.30) combined with a last-hour volume spike (z-score vs its own trailing 20-day average >= 2.0): BUY 6:01 pm New York, stop 1 x range, close 10:00 am New York - same mechanics as the other night trades. WATCH ITEM (only 25 historical occurrences, mostly overlapping the VIX night trade above) - needs ~2-4 weeks of its own live volume history before it can fire at all · v1.10 NIGHT V5: a 4th, independent night trigger (only fires when the three night trades above do not - never more than one a night), no weekday restriction, on the US Dollar Index weakening over 5 days (252-day percentile of the 5-day % change <= 0.20) combined with the market narrowing on both a 10-day AND a 20-day horizon (252-day percentile of the RSP/SPY equal-weight/cap-weight ratio's 10-day and 20-day % change, both <= 0.20): BUY 6:01 pm New York, stop 1 x range, close 10:00 am New York - same mechanics as the other night trades. WATCH ITEM (20 historical Python occurrences, 18 confirmed in MT4) - unlike Night V4, this data is available from day one, no live warm-up needed
